verdict: PREMISE (A) DISCHARGED: the weights reconstructed from the .seq statistics through compute_noise_weights() ARE the weights Siril applied — read off a planted patch to 0.0007 (Green 0.3536 actual vs 0.3537 reconstructed), with the nbstack control at 0.500 +- 0.001 proving the read-off can fail. The wnoise record's 'actual weights' (july31 0.900 ... aug14 1.094) are therefore Siril's own, and its NULL verdict stands as measured. Two facts for the registry: the weight is (scale/bgnoise)^2 on the REGISTERED image — a member's white noise is reduced by the resample (~32 % here) before it is weighted — and a planted global offset is invisible to a compose-level readout (addscale cancels it), a local patch is the readout that works.
registry_wording_one_sentence: the .seq statistics through compute_noise_weights() ARE the weights Siril applies — MEASURED by a planted-noise two-member control (`datasets/corpus/smear_attribution/noise_weight_control.json`): the noisy copy's weight read off a planted local patch 0.3536 against 0.3537 reconstructed (Green; R/B within 0.0007), the nbstack control 0.500 ± 0.001, and the weight is on the REGISTERED image's noise (a resampled white-noise copy read 3.41e-5 against 5.00e-5 unregistered).
premises_not_tested: a two-member sequence exercises the same weighting code path as 77 members (no member-count branch was seen in the source read; not exercised at n = 77 here)
the patch's 0.7 % of pixels left the IKSS location/scale of the noisy copy untouched — inferred from the nbstack readout (0.500 +- 0.001), not measured separately
the resample's -32 % on white noise generalises to other transforms only as a direction (one near-identity lanczos4 pass measured)
